text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 4

Sex almost certainly played no role against you: you are a man, the appointee is a man, and the panel was all men. An all-male panel is not evidence of bias toward a male candidate. Raising it would read as grasping and would weaken your credible points.

Your real argument is formal qualifications. You hold a master's in educational leadership and five years as deputy principal; he has "courses" and classroom experience only. If the post was advertised with leadership qualifications as a requirement or merit, the panel must justify ranking him higher.

Focus on that. Send a written follow-up citing your earlier request, set a deadline, and ask for the scoring criteria and comparative assessment.
